judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic verdict is right and I reproduced every value: problem 3's sin B = 14 sin 35 / 9 = 0.89223 giving 63.15 and 116.85 with c = 15.53 and 7.40; problem 4's A + (180 - B) = 196.65 > 180 killing the obtuse candidate and c = 13.22; problem 6's a = h = 6 giving the right angle at B and c = 10.39; problem 2's second sighting giving sin B = 1.10 > 1 and therefore no triangle; problem 10's B = 61.10 with h = 12.26. The case-rule coverage is genuinely complete — the sheet contains a zero-triangle case, an a = h borderline, four two-triangle cases and two a >= b cases — so 'independently solved all ten' and 'all three manual reasoning checks correctly distinguish zero, one, and two-triangle cases' both hold. Where I disagree is the artifact finding 'exactly ten readable worksheet problems were visually confirmed' and the accompanying visual score, which the judge attributes to sparseness. Four of the figures have measurable text collisions that the overprint gate passed. I extracted word boxes with pdftotext -bbox and rendered the pages. In problem 3 the '?' at x[337.5,343.1] y[181.9,192.5] overlaps the '9' of the second 'a = 9' label at x[339.3,345.2] y[187.8,198.4] — 30 percent of the smaller box — and the rendered page shows the question mark sitting directly on the digit. The same figure prints a second '?' at x[281.2,286.7] y[171.5,182.1], which lands on the b = 14 side line at its midpoint rather than at either B vertex. Problem 1's figure has the identical pair of faults (the '?' printed on the '6' of the second 'a = 6', overlap 0.19, and a '?' across the b = 10 line), and the same collision recurs on problem 5 ('?' over '25', 0.30) and problem 8 ('?' over '=', 0.20). tests/check_overprint.py uses OVERLAP = 0.45 of the smaller box, calibrated so subscripts do not trip it, so every one of these sits under the threshold and gate_log.txt reports 'overprint PASS'. Separately, three problems print an explanation request with no manual entry — problem 2(b) 'explain what that value tells you about this measurement', problem 6(b) 'explain why the supplement gives no second triangle in this case', and problem 7(a) 'Explain from the sizes of a and b alone why this measurement cannot be ambiguous' — so the package declares three manual items and the judge reviewed three when the worksheet prints six. Finally, problem 2's Quick Answers row is ordered against its prompt: part (a) says 'Compute h, state how many triangles are possible, and find the acute B', but the row prints '58.99, 7.71, 1.10', i.e. B before h, because verify.json declares the triangle entry first. That is the same array-order defect that produced curr-427's hard failure, here caught only because both values sit inside one part.

strengths_to_preserve: The case coverage is complete and deliberately sequenced rather than assembled: problem 1 is h < a < b (two triangles), problem 2(b) is a < h (none, exposed by sin B = 1.10 > 1), problem 6 is a = h exactly (one, right-angled at B), problems 3, 5, 8 and 9 are two-triangle cases in different contexts, and problems 4 and 7 are a >= b. Every branch of the rule stated in the directions is instantiated at least once.

Problem 6 is built as a controlled comparison with problem 1 — the worksheet says so explicitly, 'the same a and the same A as the first problem, with a longer b' — so the student sees the case flip from two triangles to one by changing a single given. That is the cleanest way to teach that h, not intuition, decides the case.

Problem 8's part (c) asks 'By how much does a exceed h? If the measurement of a shrank by exactly that much, how many triangles would remain, and what would be special about the survivor?' The excess 1.00 is machine-verified and the reasoning half is properly declared manual. It converts the case rule from a lookup into a question about measurement tolerance.

The answer key's first teaching note earns its place: 'Why h comes first: it is the only number that decides the case, and it costs one multiplication. Students who skip it end up discovering the second triangle by luck.'

The common-wrong-answers block names the two errors that define this topic: 'If they got 63.15: stopped at the acute angle and never reported the second triangle' and 'If they got 60.62: reported only the acute angle and never checked whether the supplement also fits'. Reporting a correct-looking acute angle as the whole answer is exactly the failure an ambiguous-case sheet exists to prevent.

The verification is unusually thorough for a trigonometry sheet — 36 tagged checks across ten problems, with both branches of every two-triangle case computed symbolically from the givens (e.g. '9*sin(asin(14*sin(35*pi/180)/9) - 35*pi/180)/sin(35*pi/180)' for the obtuse-branch c), rather than a rounded value being re-asserted.

root_causes.description: The SSA figure generator misplaces the '?' markers on two-triangle diagrams. Instead of sitting at the B1 and B2 vertices whose angles the problems request, one lands on the swinging side's length label and the other lands mid-way along the b side, printed across the line. The result is a question mark drawn on a digit in four of the ten figures and a stray marker on a segment the problem does not ask about.
evidence: worksheet.pdf page 3 (problem 3): word boxes '?' x[337.5,343.1] y[181.9,192.5] and '9' x[339.3,345.2] y[187.8,198.4] overlap by 30 percent of the smaller box; the rendered page shows the '?' printed on the digit.

worksheet.pdf page 3: a second '?' at x[281.2,286.7] y[171.5,182.1] sits on the segment from A x[226.9,235.7] y[198.4,209.1] to C x[338.1,346.5] y[124.3,134.9] — i.e. across the b = 14 line, at neither B vertex.

Same fault on page 1 (problem 1: '?' over '=6', overlap 0.19, plus a '?' across the b = 10 line — confirmed by rendering), page 4 (problem 5: '?' over '25', 0.30) and page 6 (problem 8: '?' over '=', 0.20).
The worksheet directions promise 'Every figure is drawn to scale from the given data, with the requested quantity marked ?', so a marker on a length the problem does not ask for actively misinforms.

root_causes.description: tests/check_overprint.py flags a collision only when the overlap exceeds 45 percent of the smaller word box. That threshold was calibrated against ordinary typesetting (subscripts, accents, radicals) where a small overlap is meaningless, but a single-glyph figure marker landing on a two-character length label produces 19 to 30 percent and passes. Figure annotations are exactly the case where a partial overlap is a defect rather than kerning, and the checker has no notion of the difference.
evidence: tests/check_overprint.py: 'OVERLAP = 0.45  # Overlap area as a fraction of the smaller box. Calibrated on 450 gated PDFs: ordinary mathematical typesetting (subscripts, accents, radicals over their argument, stacked fraction parts) produces overlaps well under this'.
The four collisions in this worksheet measure 0.19, 0.30, 0.30 and 0.20 — all below 0.45.

The checker's own docstring concedes the neighbouring blind spot: 'It cannot see a figure — a collision between two TikZ paths ... leaves no word box.' Here the boxes DO exist and are still missed, which is a threshold problem rather than the acknowledged limitation.

root_causes.description: Three problems print an explanation request that is not declared manual, so the package reports three open items when the worksheet prints six. In each case the answer key supplies the expected reasoning, so the author wrote the response without recording the slot.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 2(b): 'Compute the value the law of sines gives for sin B, and explain what that value tells you about this measurement.' verify.json id 2 has three machine entries and no manual entry.
worksheet.pdf problem 6(b): 'Find B, and explain why the supplement gives no second triangle in this case.' verify.json id 6 has three machine entries and no manual entry.
worksheet.pdf problem 7(a): 'Explain from the sizes of a and b alone why this measurement cannot be ambiguous, then find the angle at B.' verify.json id 7 has two machine entries and no manual entry.
verify.json ids 8, 9 and 10 DO carry manual entries, so the mechanism was in active use and simply not applied to 2, 6 and 7.

root_causes.description: Quick Answers rows carry up to six unlabelled values in verify.json array order, and on problem 2 that order contradicts the printed part order. Problems 8, 9 and 10 additionally mix machine entries with a declared manual entry and show no manual marker, because render_entry reaches the em-dash only when a problem has no machine-expected values at all.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers row '2. 58.99, 7.71, 1.10' against worksheet.pdf problem 2(a) 'Compute h, state how many triangles are possible, and find the acute B' — h (7.71) is asked for first and printed second, because verify.json id 2 declares the triangle entry before the h approx.
answer_key.pdf row '8. 9.00, 64.16, 115.84, 19.95, 11.23, 1.00' — six values for a three-part problem, unlabelled.
verify.json ids 8, 9, 10 each contain a manual entry; their bank rows show only numbers.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry: values joined in array order, '---' fallback guarded by 'if not vals'.

improvements.title: Fix '?' marker placement on two-triangle SSA figures so it sits at the requested vertex, not on the swing-side label or across the b side
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_figures.py, anchor each '?' marker to the vertex or segment it annotates rather than to an offset from the swinging side, and place it on the outward bisector of that vertex's angle at a radius that clears the existing angle arc. Then run a post-placement collision pass over all figure annotations for a single figure — every label and marker has a known box in figure coordinates — and nudge along the bisector until no two boxes overlap, failing the build if a placement cannot be found. Note that this is the same code path as the known swing-side-label defect; the manifestation here is a marker landing on a length label and a marker crossing the b side rather than a label crossing the base line, but the fix is one placement routine.
improvements.regression_test: Generate the figure for curr-428 problem 3 (A = 35, b = 14, a = 9, two triangles) and assert that no two annotation boxes overlap at all, and that each '?' box lies within a small radius of the vertex it annotates (B1 and B2), not within the bounding box of any 'a = ...' label and not on the segment AC. The assertion fails today on both counts. Repeat for A = 30 with b = 10 and b = 18 to cover problems 1 and 8.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a printed question mark drawn on a digit from four of this worksheet's ten figures, and removes a marker that points at a quantity the problem does not ask for — which on a sheet whose directions promise 'the requested quantity marked ?' is actively misleading. Applies to every ambiguous-SSA figure the renderer produces.
improvements.risk: A collision-avoidance pass can push markers far enough from their vertex to become ambiguous about what they annotate, especially on narrow triangles where several annotations compete for the same wedge; the nudge should be bounded and the build should fail rather than silently place a marker far away.

improvements.title: Apply a stricter overprint threshold to figure annotations than to body typesetting
improvements.proposed_change: Give tests/check_overprint.py a second, tighter threshold for word boxes that fall inside a figure region, since the 0.45 fraction is calibrated for subscripts and radicals in flowing text and has no counterpart inside a diagram, where any overlap between two independent annotations is a defect. Identify figure regions from the generated figs_*.tex bounding boxes (or from a marker the renderer emits), and use an overlap fraction near 0.05 there. Report the offending pair with coordinates so the author can find it on the page.
improvements.regression_test: Run the checker over curr-428's worksheet.pdf and assert it reports the four collisions on pages 1, 3, 4 and 6 (fractions 0.19, 0.30, 0.30, 0.20). Today it exits 0. Assert it still passes a control PDF containing ordinary subscripts and stacked fractions in body text, so the existing calibration on the 450-document corpus is not disturbed.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the gap between what the overprint gate promises and what it detects. The checker exists because three collisions shipped with clean logs; this is a fourth class it currently reports as clean.
improvements.risk: Legitimate figure typesetting does contain small overlaps — a degree symbol against its number, a subscripted vertex label such as B_2 — so the tight threshold needs the same kind of calibration pass over the existing corpus before it hard-fails, or it will produce noise on every diagram.

improvements.title: Declare the explanation halves of problems 2(b), 6(b) and 7(a) as manual items
improvements.proposed_change: Require a manual verify entry for every printed request whose answer is a sentence, including when it is attached to a computed part of the same problem. Enforce it with a lint over the worksheet source that matches explanation imperatives ('explain what ...', 'explain why ...', 'explain from ... why ...') and fails when the corresponding verify id has no manual entry. This worksheet is the clean test case: three problems already carry correct manual declarations, so the rule needs only to extend the existing practice consistently.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture from curr-428 problem 6: prompt containing 'explain why the supplement gives no second triangle in this case' with a verify id holding three machine entries and no manual entry. The gate must exit non-zero naming the unflagged explanation and pass once a manual entry is added; assert a full curr-428-shaped fixture's manual count rises from 3 to 6.
improvements.expected_impact: Doubles the honestly declared open surface on this sheet, and on an ambiguous-case worksheet the explanations are the assessed skill — deciding how many triangles exist and saying why is the entire topic.
improvements.risk: Text scanning over-triggers on instructional asides and under-triggers on justifications phrased as questions; needs an author override and calibration against baseline worksheets before it hard-fails.

improvements.title: Label bank values by sub-part and emit them in printed order, not verify.json array order
improvements.proposed_change: Add a required 'slot' field to verify entries on multi-entry problems and have scripts/render_quick_answers.py print labelled values in the worksheet's part order. Add a gate that compares the number of bank values against the number of printed sub-parts and fails when a slot is missing or duplicated. This case shows why order cannot be inferred: problem 2 declares the triangle entry before the height, and the row prints B before h although the prompt asks for h first.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture from curr-428 problem 2: prompt asking for h, then the triangle count, then the acute B, with verify entries declared triangle-first. Assert the rendered row reads 'h = 7.71; B = 58.99; sin B = 1.10' rather than the current '58.99, 7.71, 1.10'. Add a case from problem 8 (six values across three parts) asserting each value carries its part label.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the ordering hazard that produced curr-427's hard failure, and makes rows like '8. 9.00, 64.16, 115.84, 19.95, 11.23, 1.00' usable — six unlabelled numbers across three parts is not a grading aid.
improvements.risk: Requires slot fields on existing verify.json files; inferring them from order reintroduces the assumption being removed, so migration should be a one-time author-reviewed pass. Labelled rows are wider and will reduce the bank's column count.

improvements.title: Show a manual-review marker on Quick Answers rows that mix machine and manual entries
improvements.proposed_change: Change scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry so a problem whose entry list contains a type == 'manual' appends an explicit marker to its bank row, rather than reaching the manual em-dash only when the problem has no machine entries at all. Print a one-line legend beneath the bank.
improvements.regression_test: Render curr-428's verify.json ids 8, 9 and 10 (each mixing machine entries with a manual entry) and assert every one of the three bank rows carries a manual marker. All three render today as bare number lists, so the assertion fails before the fix; assert a manual-only problem still renders the plain em-dash.
improvements.expected_impact: All three of this sheet's correctly declared manual items are currently invisible in the grading column — the one place a teacher looks first. The marker makes the author's good declaration practice visible to the person who needs it.
improvements.risk: Extra row width reduces the adaptive column count on dense sheets; use a single glyph.

case_summary: An unusually complete treatment of the ambiguous SSA case: every branch of the h-versus-a-versus-b rule appears at least once, problem 6 is a controlled variant of problem 1 that flips the case by changing a single given, and problem 8 turns the rule into a measurement-tolerance question. The mathematics is correct throughout — I recomputed all 36 checks' worth of values, including both branches of every two-triangle case — and the verification is genuinely thorough, computing each obtuse-branch side symbolically from the givens rather than re-asserting a rounded number. ACCEPT is right. Two findings sit under the score. First, four of the ten figures print a '?' marker on top of a length label (19 to 30 percent box overlap, confirmed by pdftotext -bbox and by rendering pages 1 and 3), and the same figures print a second '?' across the b side at a point neither problem asks about; tests/check_overprint.py misses all of it because its 0.45 threshold is calibrated for subscripts in body text, not for annotations inside a diagram. Second, problems 2(b), 6(b) and 7(a) each print an explanation request with no manual entry, so the package declares three open items on a sheet that prints six — notable because ids 8, 9 and 10 are declared correctly, making this an inconsistency rather than an omission of practice. Problem 2's bank row also prints B before h against the prompt's order, the same array-order defect that caused curr-427's hard failure.
